- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict (forecast too low) — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model tends to lag — forecast should align with 5-day SMA or 7-day EWMA.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model often misjudges direction — use sentiment momentum (e.g., 3-day average) to weight directionality.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If true outcome shows a “tail” or “late surge” (e.g., last 3–5 days > 90% of 30-day mean), model often misses it — forecast last 5 days should be adjusted upward by 1–3% of recent volatility.
